entities.summary:
William Sharp Macleay (1819-1865) was a British civil servant and entomologist who promoted the Quinarian system of classification. He served as the Director of the Entomological Society of London from 1847 to 1856. Macleay's work in the field of entomology contributed to the development of modern taxonomy.

Macleay's classification system was based on the number of wings, with the most primitive species having two wings and the most advanced having four wings. His system was initially met with skepticism but eventually gained acceptance among entomologists.

Macleay's legacy extends beyond his classification system. He was a pioneer in the field of entomological research and was instrumental in the establishment of the Entomological Society of London. His work laid the foundation for future generations of entomologists and contributed to our understanding of the natural world.

The Quinarian system of classification is still used today in the field of entomology, although it has been modified and expanded upon. Macleay's work continues to be celebrated as a significant contribution to the field of entomology and taxonomy.
